builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ORION: An Outcome-Driven LLM Advisor for RL-Based Multi-Domain 6G Slice Placement
summary: The method replaces a memoryless LLM placement planner (or FIFO episodic store) with an outcome-driven episodic memory that records network-condition profiles, proposed plans, and verified feasibility outcomes, feeding labelled successes and failures back to the planner. It costs memory infrastructure to store and retrieve episode records, plus a feasibility-verification step per completed attempt, and it presumes a downstream multi-agent RL coordinator that treats plans as soft priors. It can fail when deployment conditions drift from recorded profiles, when importance-based retention discards rare but critical failure modes, or when the domain-specific RL execution layer cannot be reproduced, since the gain was demonstrated only within a simulated 6G slice-placement environment.
rationale: The technique is a well-motivated memory pattern for LLM planners, but the reported gains are confined to a specialized telecom orchestration stack with an RL execution layer, so the reader should track it rather than adopt it directly.
technique: Outcome-driven episodic memory for LLM planners

claims.statement: The method replaces a memoryless LLM placement planner (or FIFO episodic store) with an outcome-driven episodic memory that records network-condition profiles, proposed plans, and verified feasibility outcomes, feeding labelled successes and failures back to the planner. It costs memory infrastructure to store and retrieve episode records, plus a feasibility-verification step per completed attempt, and it presumes a downstream multi-agent RL coordinator that treats plans as soft priors. It can fail when deployment conditions drift from recorded profiles, when importance-based retention discards rare but critical failure modes, or when the domain-specific RL execution layer cannot be reproduced, since the gain was demonstrated only within a simulated 6G slice-placement environment.

On held-out topology families, the memory improves admission by 4.6-11.5 percentage points over the same planner without memory, with importance-based retention accounting for most of the improvement over FIFO.
